# Interest Rates Model

This document replicates an earlier vector autoregression (VAR) forecast of commercial real estate cap rates that uses the 10-year Treasury yield (DGS10) and the federal funds rate (DFF) as predictors. It tests how well that forecast held up from April 2023 to March 2024, then re-estimates the model on the full sample and forecasts 12 months ahead.

The model exists to forecast **cap rates**. The interest rate forecasts are inputs to the model, so their accuracy is reported but is not the goal.

## Setup

### Load packages

```{r}
#| message: false
library(vars)
library(tseries)
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(readxl)
```

### Settings

```{r}
data_path <- here("Data", "newfinal_monthly_all.xlsx")
if (!file.exists(data_path)) {
  stop("Data file not found: ", data_path,
       "\nPlace newfinal_monthly_all.xlsx in a Data/ folder at the project root.")
}

diff_order <- 2   # order of differencing applied to DGS10 and DFF
p_lag      <- 4   # VAR lag order (compare with the VARselect output below)
n_ahead    <- 12  # forecast horizon in months
```

### Import data

Expected columns: `observation_date`, `cap` (cap rate), `DGS10`, `DFF`. Monthly, April 2013 to March 2024.

```{r}
dat <- read_excel(data_path) |>
  transmute(
    observation_date = as.Date(observation_date),
    CapRate = cap,
    DGS10   = DGS10,
    DFF     = DFF
  ) |>
  arrange(observation_date)

expected_months <- seq(as.Date("2013-04-01"), as.Date("2024-03-01"), by = "month")
stopifnot(
  !anyNA(dat),
  nrow(dat) == length(expected_months),
  all(format(dat$observation_date, "%Y-%m") == format(expected_months, "%Y-%m"))
)

levels_ts <- ts(as.matrix(dat[, c("CapRate", "DGS10", "DFF")]),
                start = c(2013, 4), frequency = 12)
```

## Prepare model data

DGS10 and DFF are differenced to make them stationary.

```{r}
model_ts <- ts.intersect(
  CapRate = levels_ts[, "CapRate"],
  DGS10   = diff(levels_ts[, "DGS10"], differences = diff_order),
  DFF     = diff(levels_ts[, "DFF"],   differences = diff_order)
)
```

Stationarity check (augmented Dickey-Fuller; small p-values support stationarity):

```{r}
round(sapply(colnames(model_ts), function(v) adf.test(model_ts[, v])$p.value), 3)
```

### Split into training and test periods

```{r}
train_end  <- c(2023, 3)
test_start <- c(2023, 4)

old_model_ts <- window(model_ts,  end   = train_end)    # model inputs, through Mar 2023
old_levels   <- window(levels_ts, end   = train_end)    # levels, used to rebuild forecasts
actual       <- window(levels_ts, start = test_start)   # actual levels, Apr 2023 to Mar 2024

actual_df <- bind_cols(
  tibble(observation_date = seq(as.Date("2023-04-01"), by = "month", length.out = n_ahead)),
  as_tibble(as.data.frame(actual))
)
```

## Helper functions

```{r}
# Rebuild levels from forecasted differences using the last observed levels
undiff <- function(fc_diff, last_levels, d = diff_order) {
  diffinv(fc_diff, differences = d, xi = tail(last_levels, d))[-seq_len(d)]
}

# Turn a vars::predict() result into a tidy data frame of forecast levels
forecast_to_levels <- function(fc, history_levels, start_date) {
  tibble(
    observation_date = seq(start_date, by = "month", length.out = n_ahead),
    CapRate_fcst  = fc$fcst$CapRate[, "fcst"],
    CapRate_lower = fc$fcst$CapRate[, "lower"],
    CapRate_upper = fc$fcst$CapRate[, "upper"],
    DGS10_fcst    = undiff(fc$fcst$DGS10[, "fcst"], history_levels[, "DGS10"]),
    DFF_fcst      = undiff(fc$fcst$DFF[, "fcst"],   history_levels[, "DFF"])
  )
}
```

## Build model (old)

```{r}
lag_old <- VARselect(old_model_ts, lag.max = 15, type = "const")
lag_old$selection
```

```{r}
old_model <- VAR(old_model_ts, p = p_lag, type = "const")
```

## Forecast (old)

```{r}
old_fc <- predict(old_model, n.ahead = n_ahead, ci = 0.95)
fc_old <- forecast_to_levels(old_fc, old_levels, as.Date("2023-04-01"))
fc_old
```

## Compare old forecast to actual values

### Line graphs

```{r}
plot_forecast <- function(var, ribbon = FALSE) {
  p <- ggplot()
  if (ribbon) {
    p <- p + geom_ribbon(
      data = fc_old,
      aes(x = observation_date, ymin = .data[[paste0(var, "_lower")]],
          ymax = .data[[paste0(var, "_upper")]]),
      fill = "blue", alpha = 0.12
    )
  }
  p +
    geom_line(data = fc_old,
              aes(x = observation_date, y = .data[[paste0(var, "_fcst")]], color = "Forecast")) +
    geom_line(data = actual_df,
              aes(x = observation_date, y = .data[[var]], color = "Actual")) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c(Forecast = "blue", Actual = "red")) +
    labs(title = paste(var, "forecast vs. actual"), x = NULL, y = var, color = NULL)
}
```

```{r}
plot_forecast("CapRate", ribbon = TRUE)
```

```{r}
plot_forecast("DGS10")
```

```{r}
plot_forecast("DFF")
```

### Forecast accuracy

Absolute error by month, then summary measures for each variable. MAPE uses the actual value in the denominator.

```{r}
comparison <- inner_join(fc_old, actual_df, by = "observation_date")

abs_errors <- tibble(
  observation_date = comparison$observation_date,
  CapRate = abs(comparison$CapRate - comparison$CapRate_fcst),
  DGS10   = abs(comparison$DGS10   - comparison$DGS10_fcst),
  DFF     = abs(comparison$DFF     - comparison$DFF_fcst)
)
abs_errors
```

```{r}
accuracy <- map_dfr(c("CapRate", "DGS10", "DFF"), function(v) {
  a <- comparison[[v]]
  f <- comparison[[paste0(v, "_fcst")]]
  tibble(
    variable = v,
    MAE      = mean(abs(a - f)),
    MAPE_pct = 100 * mean(abs((a - f) / a))
  )
})
accuracy
```

## Build model (new)

Re-estimate on the full sample (April 2013 to March 2024).

```{r}
lag_new <- VARselect(model_ts, lag.max = 15, type = "const")
lag_new$selection
```

```{r}
new_model <- VAR(model_ts, p = p_lag, type = "const")
```

## Forecast (new)

```{r}
new_fc <- predict(new_model, n.ahead = n_ahead, ci = 0.95)
fc_new <- forecast_to_levels(new_fc, levels_ts, as.Date("2024-04-01"))
fc_new
```

```{r}
history <- tibble(observation_date = dat$observation_date, CapRate = dat$CapRate)

ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = history, aes(x = observation_date, y = CapRate)) +
  geom_ribbon(data = fc_new,
              aes(x = observation_date, ymin = CapRate_lower, ymax = CapRate_upper),
              fill = "blue", alpha = 0.12) +
  geom_line(data = fc_new, aes(x = observation_date, y = CapRate_fcst), color = "blue") +
  labs(title = "Cap rate: history and 12-month forecast", x = NULL, y = "Cap rate")
```

## Limitations

-   The cap rate is modeled in levels while DGS10 and DFF are second-differenced. Test whether this mix is appropriate (for example with the ADF results above, or by trying first differences).
-   Forecast intervals are shown for the cap rate only. Intervals for DGS10 and DFF are not shown because they are produced on the differenced scale.
-   The lag order is set to `p_lag`. Compare it with the `VARselect` criteria above and document the choice.
-   With one 12-month test window, MAE and MAPE are a small sample of forecast performance.
